hook_text: Touch a resistor to a leg and an LED lights from a current far too small to light it. That leg is the base.
clip_script: Three legs: collector, base, emitter. Check the card. Load and positive to the collector, emitter to negative. Nothing into the base: off. A trickle into the base through a resistor of tens of kilohms: on, and a hundred times that trickle flows collector to emitter. The LED lights. That is a switch with no moving parts. Hang an LDR on the base and daylight switches it; swap the LDR with the resistor and darkness switches it. A night light. Vary the base gently instead and the collector copies it, bigger: an amplifier. Always a base resistor. Always check the legs. Under 100 milliamps for a BC547.
visual_style: Whiteboard transistor symbol with legs labelled; a finger touching a resistor to the base and an LED lighting; an LDR swapped with a resistor and a moon icon; a small wave becoming a big wave; a card showing C B E.
mood: Curious and precise, like a first breadboard success.
pacing: Legs, off, trickle, on, LDR, swap, amplifier, rules.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the touch-to-light circuit with a 100 kilohm base resistor.
